title: Quasi-affineness can be checked on an affine target cover
statement: Let $h:Z\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $S=\bigcup_{a\in A}S_a$ be an affine open cover. A quasi-affine scheme means a scheme isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme, where quasi-compact means that every open covering admits a finite subcover. Then $h$ is quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism] if and only if $h^{-1}(S_a)$ is a quasi-affine scheme for every $a\in A$. No quasi-compactness or separation hypothesis on $S$ and no finite-type hypothesis on $h$ is imposed.

proof.text: The forward implication is immediate from [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]: if $h$ is quasi-affine, then the inverse image of every affine open of $S$, in particular each $S_a$, is a quasi-affine scheme.

Assume that every $Z_a=h^{-1}(S_a)$ is quasi-affine. By [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding], each $Z_a$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The restricted map $h_a:Z_a\to S_a$ is therefore quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) (its target is affine and hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]); applying [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target] to the affine cover $(S_a)$ gives that $h$ is quasi-compact. To see that $h$ is quasi-separated, cover $Z\times_S Z$ by the opens $Z_a\times_{S_a}Z_a$. The inverse image of the $a$-th open under the diagonal is $Z_a$, and the restricted diagonal is the diagonal of $h_a$, which is quasi-compact because $h_a$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). The same target-local criterion [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target] applied to $\Delta_h$ makes $\Delta_h$ quasi-compact; by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], $h$ is quasi-separated. (If the cover is empty, then $S$ and $Z$ are empty and the conclusion is vacuous.)

source.place: Tag 01SM, proof of lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, (2) implies (4), first paragraph; Schemes Lemma 01KO for the diagonal locality

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=h_*\mathcal O_Z$ with its natural $\mathcal O_S$-algebra structure. Since $h$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] makes its underlying module quasi-coherent. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2) to obtain the affine morphism $\pi:Y=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)\to S$ and an algebra isomorphism $\alpha:\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_*\mathcal O_Y$, with each $Y_a=\pi^{-1}(S_a)$ affine and identified with $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(S_a)$.

source.place: Tag 01SM, proof of lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, (2) implies (4), construction of $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_X$ and the relative spectrum

proof.text: Use the inverse algebra map $\alpha^{-1}:\pi_*\mathcal O_Y\to h_*\mathcal O_Z$ in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-algebra-local-maps]. For every $a$ it gives a morphism $c_a:Z_a\to Y$ over $S$, and the maps agree on all overlaps. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] they glue to $c:Z\to Y$ with $\pi c=h$. The restriction $c_a$ factors through $Y_a$. Under the affine chart $Y_a\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(S_a)$, the induced map on global sections is $\alpha_a^{-1}\alpha_a=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A(S_a)}$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] identifies this restriction with the canonical map $j_a:Z_a\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(Z_a,\mathcal O_{Z_a})$.

source.place: Tag 01SM, proof of lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, (2) implies (4), canonical morphism and its affine-chart restriction

proof.text: Each $j_a$ is an open immersion by [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding], so the composite $Z_a\hookrightarrow Z\xrightarrow{c}Y$ is an open immersion into the open subscheme $Y_a$. To check that $c$ is injective on points, suppose $c(z)=c(z')=y$. Since $\pi c=h$, both $z$ and $z'$ map to $\pi(y)\in S$. Choose $a$ with $\pi(y)\in S_a$. Then both points lie in $Z_a$, and injectivity of $j_a$ gives $z=z'$. Thus $c$ is injective on points. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-injective-local-source] makes $c$ an open immersion. It is quasi-compact: $Z_a=c^{-1}(Y_a)$ is quasi-compact, while $Y_a$ is affine and hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $c|_{Z_a}:Z_a\to Y_a$ quasi-compact; [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target] then makes $c$ quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 01SM, proof of lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, (2) implies (4), local open immersion and quasi-compactness

proof.text: For any affine open $U\subseteq S$, the relative-Spec chart in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2) makes $Y_U=\pi^{-1}(U)$ affine. Since $c$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and $\pi c=h$, the inverse image $h^{-1}(U)=c^{-1}(Y_U)$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme of the affine scheme $Y_U$. By [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism], this is exactly that $h$ is quasi-affine.
